results.title: A Primer on Uncertainty and Calibration in Deep Learning
results.content: For example, instead of saying: *“The house price is 480,000,”a well-calibrated model would say: “The price is 480,000 ± 70,000 , but I’m really not confident because the location is novel to me.” And that ± 70,000 is where uncertainty kicks in.* Hence, uncertainty in deep learning is the **lack of confidence a model has in its predictions**, typically arising from **incomplete information, ambiguous data, or limitations in the model itself** (this shouldn’t be confused with confidence value model gives as output, though ideally it should, this discrepancy in expected and actual behaviour of model logits/probability/scores is comes under model calibration, this also will be covered in latter sections). A deterministic model makes a point prediction `y=f(x`), but a probabilistic or uncertainty-aware model outputs a **distribution** over possible predictions: `y∼p(y∣x).` Uncertainty is then quantified via: * **Variance**, entropy, or confidence intervals in regression * **Predictive entropy** or margin in classification That said, lets start diving into core concepts. ### Method 1 : Maximum Likelihood Estimation (MLE) This simplest way of modelling this type of uncertainty is by predicting not just a mean output `μ(x)` but also a corresponding variance `σ2(x)`, treating the output as a Gaussian distribution: \(y^∼N(μ(x),σ2(x))\) During training, we use *Maximum Likelihood Estimation (MLE)*, leading to the following Negative Log-Likelihood (NLL) loss: \(\mathcal{L}\_{\text{NLL}} = \frac{1}{2\sigma²(x)} (y -\mu(x))² + \frac{1}{2} \log \sigma²(x)\) This formulation naturally balances error (left term) and uncertainty (right term containing `σ)`. Conversely, a model may express confident predictions (low uncertainty) but be overconfident and hence **badly mis-calibrated**. #### Ensembles and Dropout Both methods, discussed earlier for epistemic uncertainty, naturally improve calibration: * **Ensembles** smooth out extreme predictions across models * **Dropout at test time** simulates stochastic ensembles These methods reduce **variance** and act as regularizers, especially useful when used with temperature scaling. #### Prediction Interval Plots For regression models, especially those predicting both mean and variance (e.g., heteroscedastic regression), we can plot: * Confidence intervals (e.g., 90%, 95%) This reveals how uncertainty expands or contracts with input domain shifts, and whether **the intervals actually cover the target**, which speaks to coverage and calibration.

results.title: Calibrating LLMs with Information- Theoretic Evidential Deep Learning
results.content: Evidential Deep Learning (EDL), an uncertainty-aware approach, enables uncertainty estimation in a single forward pass, making it a promising method for calibrating fine-tuned LLMs. However, despite its computational efficiency, EDL is prone to overfitting, as its training objective can result in overly concentrated probability distributions. However, these approaches typically require multiple forward passes, significantly increasing the inference time for LLMs. Evidential Deep Learning (EDL) (Sensoy et al., 2018; Malinin & Gales, 2018) offers a more efficient alternative by providing uncertainty estimates with a single forward pass. Despite its success in various tasks, recent studies (Deng et al., 2023; Chen et al., 2024) indicate that EDL can still yield overconfident predictions which leads to inaccurate uncertainty estimates, degrading the model’s calibration performance. Baselines: We compare our method against a variety of baselines, including standard MAP training, two conventional uncertainty-aware approaches: Deep Ensemble (Ens) (Lakshminarayanan et al., 2017; Fort et al., 2019) and MC-Dropout (MCD) (Gal & Ghahramani, 2016), and Laplace-LoRA (LA) (Yang et al., 2024), a recent calibration method tailored for fine-tuned LLMs. Additionally, we include four baselines from the EDL family: vanilla EDL (Sensoy et al., 2018), VID (Chen et al., 2018) from VB-based EDL, and two SOTA methods: I-EDL (Deng et al., 2023) and R-EDL (Chen et al., 2024). The superior performance of IB-EDL, compared to other EDL methods, can be attributed to the regularization in Eq. 14, which discourages the model from generating excessively large evidences that lead to over-concentrated Dirichlet distributions. EDL: EDL leverages models to predict the Dirichlet prior distribution, with training typically done using NLL (Haussmann et al., 2023), -loss (Tsiligkaridis, 2021), or MSE (Sensoy et al., 2018). Other uncertainty-aware methods: Besides EDL, there are other methods for uncertainty estimation and calibration, including Bayesian Neural Networks via Variational Inference (Graves, 2011; Blundell et al., 2015), MC-Dropout (Gal & Ghahramani, 2016), stochastic gradient MCMC (Welling & Teh, 2011; Ma et al., 2015), and Laplace approximations (Ritter et al., 2018; Kristiadi et al., 2021), recently extended to LoRA fine-tuned LLMs (Yang et al., 2024; Wang et al., 2024a; Li et al., 2024). Our method, IB-EDL, introduces minimal computational overhead while significantly improving calibration in fine-tuned LLMs. Additionally, IB-EDL maintains model performance even in the presence of substantial label noise.

results.title: Deep Evidential Learning for Dose Prediction
results.content: We found that (i)epistemic uncertainty was highly correlated with prediction errors, with various association indices comparable or stronger than those for Monte-Carlo Dropout and Deep Ensemble methods, (ii)the median error varied with uncertainty threshold much more linearly for epistemic uncertainty in Deep Evidential Learning relative to these other two conventional frameworks, indicative of a more uniformly calibrated sensitivity to model errors, (iii)relative to epistemic uncertainty, aleatoric uncertainty demonstrated a more significant shift in its distribution in response to Gaussian noise added to CT intensity, compatible with its interpretation as reflecting data noise. The results in Table 1 indicated that, at least compared to Monte-Carlo Dropout and Deep Ensemble methods, Deep Evidential Learning model appeared to yield spectra of uncertainty values which were strongly correlated with prediction error, indicating that it could enact a feasible uncertainty estimation framework that helps to discover and highlight potential regions of ignorance within the deep learning model.
